title: D365 Architect table definition
description: Declarative YAML shape for a Dynamics table, produced by `d365architect table export`.

entity.description: The table's logical name, e.g. "account". Serialises as the top-level "entity" key.

schemaName.description: The customization-prefixed schema name, e.g. "new_BankAccount". Fixed at creation time — required when creating a table, immutable after.

ownershipType.description: "UserOwned", "OrganizationOwned", etc. Required to create a table; can't be changed afterwards.

isActivity.description: Only present when true — false is the platform default for a table.

hasActivities.description: Only present when true — false is the platform default for a table.

hasNotes.description: Only present when true — false is the platform default for a table.

schemaName.description: The customization-prefixed schema name, e.g. "new_BankName". Required to create a column; immutable after.

physicalName.description: The underlying SQL column name from a legacy unpacked solution's Entity.xml, when it differs from Name in more than casing. Only ever set by EntityXmlDefinitionReader — the live Web API has no equivalent concept (Dataverse manages its own storage rather than mapping columns onto SQL Server directly).

requiredLevel.description: "recommended", "applicationrequired" or "systemrequired". Only present when set to something other than "none" — that's Dataverse's default for every column type.

precision.description: Decimal places. For Money, only meaningful when PrecisionSource is 2 (attribute-specific).

precisionSource.description: Money only: 0 = currency-specific, 1 = organization setting, 2 = this attribute's own Precision.

targets.description: Lookup/Customer/Owner: logical names of the table(s) this column can point to.

isCustomField.description: Only present when true — false (a standard, non-custom field) is by far the common case.
